column40: Strongest supported reading: Public already-promoted project documents attach, to named METR company-identifying engagements, only the terms those documents themselves state. FRR (published 2026-05-19) records that METR did not request or receive compensation, that participants provided complimentary model access, that no applicable personnel CoI policy was in force at project start, that the pilot was not compliant with all AEF-1 requirements, that remaining participants could redact certain findings but not the top-level redaction-summary sentence, and that they did not have approval rights over the industry-level report [MDQ0063,MDQ0044,MDQ0048,MDQ0004,MDQ0005,MDQ0016,MDP0256]. The Hugging Face incident PDF (published 2026-08-26) records that METR did not take payment from OpenAI, accepted free API credits, and that OpenAI could redact any non-public information and gave feedback beyond redaction [MDQ0102,MDQ0006,MDQ0007]. GPT-5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.1-Codex-Max and gpt-oss posts record a standard NDA and OpenAI comms/legal review and approval of the public post [MDQ0008,MDQ0009,MDQ0010,MDQ0025,MDQ0103,MDQ0104,MDQ0105,MDQ0106]. The Anthropic Opus 4.6 sabotage-review PDF records a mutual NDA, publication review, redaction control, and a general ability to veto publication of METR's review [MDQ0023,MDQ0024,MDQ0027]. METR CoI policy version 1.0 is dated 28 August 2026, after FRR publication and after HF publication [MDQ0014,MDQ0046,MDQ0095,MDT0138]. These are document-stated terms. They are not a finding about any person's or organization's motive.
